question: Should OpenClaw publish a public OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and should it be a static artifact, an authenticated runtime endpoint, or a documented TypeBox/JSON Schema generation path instead?
rationale: This would stabilize external API, auth, scope, plugin-surface, and versioning behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, auth boundary, versioning model, and compatibility checks before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Static Artifact
options.body: Publish a generated, versioned schema artifact for client generation without adding a runtime schema endpoint yet.

options.title: Defer To Existing Protocol Docs
options.body: Close later only if maintainers decide the TypeBox/JSON Schema pipeline plus Gateway protocol docs are the intended client-generation surface.

recommendation.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, auth boundary, versioning model, and compatibility checks before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the closest prior OpenAPI/schema artifact work and recent Gateway auth history, so he is the best available owner for the product/API boundary question.
